title: Choose the visual world (bolder hand)
question: Bolder hand: foreign forms at full commitment. The deal led with the Quiz Issue. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Camilo Issue
options.lineage: 1990s teen-magazine quiz spreads: torn halftone collage, lettered checkboxes, a verdict box at the fold
options.thesis: The portfolio is a magazine issue about Camilo, and the hero is a quiz, 'Are you hiring a Camilo?', whose verdict box is the CV.
options.viewport: Masthead 'THE CAMILO ISSUE' at a tilt, a torn halftone portrait taped in, a three-question quiz whose answers map to MAGI, Ghost Layer and 'keeps learning', and a verdict box that opens to the CV download.
options.risk: The most fun and the most on-voice, but teen-mag energy can read unserious to a recruiter if the type and grid are not strict; acid green replaces the mag's pink+green pair to keep one main colour.

raised.raise: One statement per spread: vast quiet space around each feature, so the collage never becomes noise.
Every item carries a small ticket of origin: repo link, language, year.

options.label: Live Glyph Render
options.lineage: ASCII renderers: glyph density standing in for light
options.thesis: Your portrait and your projects rendered live as characters; the whole site sits on one strict monospace grid, and the ASCII is the image, never a background.
options.viewport: Left: your portrait as a live glyph render that turns with the pointer. Right: name in the same grid, one line, numbered project rows, '> download cv'; keyboard-letter nav along the bottom.
options.case: Beats the quiz on both axes: it is literally the ASCII you asked for, and a monospace grid scans fast for recruiters.
options.risk: The closest to a terminal costume; it stays honest only if ASCII lives in the render plates and text stays calm and readable.

options.label: Safelight Darkroom
options.thesis: Dithering as development: your portrait emerges in the tray as a dot screen while the timer runs, and the page moves through stations (expose, develop, fix, wash, dry).
options.viewport: A developing tray holds your portrait, its dither threshold sweeping in as the timer counts; name and one line beside it, a station strip, 'Pull the print (CV)'.
options.case: Beats the quiz on both axes: the develop reveal makes dithering the hero mechanic, and ordered stations map cleanly to sections.
options.risk: An amber wash everywhere can go monotonous and low-contrast; Day mode needs the 'lights on' room to stay legible.

options.label: Fashion Flagship
options.thesis: Projects as looks in a slow lookbook.
options.viewport: One huge word, one full-bleed image.
options.case: Fuses poorly: needs photography you do not have, and luxury is off-voice for 'just a boring person'.
options.kept: One statement per spread with vast quiet space.

options.label: Moon-shadow Bazaar
options.thesis: Projects traded as shadows at stalls.
options.viewport: A lane of stalls under the moon.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the metaphor hides what the projects do.
options.kept: Every item carries a ticket of origin.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dev portfolio everyone recognises, executed impeccably, with dither as accent tiles.
canonCard.viewport: Nav, avatar, name, one-line bio, CV button, a dithered tile beside it and a bento row of projects below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other dev portfolios by design, which is the 'generic dev template' you said would feel wrong.
